tmn.review:
Course - POL101


Faculty's Initial: TmN (Tasmia Nower)


The experience may vary from person to person. I am just sharing my experience.

Well, I have seen a lot of negative reviews about TmN ma’am saying “Drop for God sake”, “Worst”, “Course ta hell kore dibe”, etc. I was asking people if it is possible to get an A under her? Unfortunately, I didn't get any positive answer. Finally, one person told me that with effort and following her instructions, it is possible to score an A. So, I continued with TmN ma’am, and it was the best decision I have ever made in my NSU life.

I have never studied political science before, so I had literally zero knowledge about it. In the first class, she ensured that we didn't necessarily need prior knowledge of political science. She suggested keeping an eye on what is happening in the world and staying updated.
POL101 is an elementary course. This course covers topics such as power, types of power, state, unitary systems, federal systems, political ideologies, regimes, constitutions and rights, legislatures, executives, and bureaucracies the judiciary branch, International relations, and the United Nations.

Tasmia ma’am is really great at teaching, and she is so passionate about this subject. Also, she is so friendly towards the students. In the first class, she played a game called “Ice-breaking session,” where all the students got to know each other, which was both very engaging and enjoyable.
She plays short videos about different topics in class and discusses those, which were very interesting from my point of view and unique as well. She explained each topic in detail, using relevant examples to illustrate her points. Her slides are compact and very precise which made studying more manageable. Additionally, reading her slides was enough to ace the exams. Her explanation was excellent; I really fell in love with political science because of her. She is the definition of beauty with a brain.

Besides explaining the slides, she always adds some extra information that is very important. I suggest that anyone who wants to do well on the quiz should take note of it, as there will be 2-3 questions, such as “According to class discussion,” which will be the correct answer. — like that.

She took two presentations, one is a mini presentation and the other is a formal presentation. Both the presentations were “Group Presentation”. For her mini-presentation, she uploaded several short videos, including ones on Palestine-Israel, Catalonia, and Russia-Ukraine, among others. We had the freedom to choose our topic. For mini-presentations, no slides were required, and no formal attire was necessary.
She meticulously wrote down every detail of the speakers during the presentation and provided feedback in the next class.
She is so serious about presentations, as she said several times, “I love presentations.” So, make sure you have a great team to ace the presentation.

For the final presentation, she uploaded a guideline on the “Canvas” where everything was written clearly, including Dos and Don’ts and marking criteria. Formal attire was mandatory, as were the slides.

She took four quizzes and counted the best three. There were MCQs and T/F in the quiz. Furthermore, the mid and the final had the same pattern, 15 marks of MCQs and T/F, and one argumentative open-ended question. We had to write one out of two. She checked the exam scripts generously. If one writes exact points by avoiding irrelevant topics, it is very much possible to score full marks.

She is so strict about attendance. If anyone missed one class, she deducted one mark from attendance. Also, please try not to be late to class, as she may not consider your attendance.

She curved one grade, and I can vouch for it as I have several friends in the same section. Try to be in her good books. Also, try to respond to her questions that she asks during the lecture.

Exams and assessments:

Quiz - 10% ( counted best 3 out of 4)
Mid - 25%
Mini Presentation - 10%
Final Presentation - 20%
Attendance - 10%
Final - 25%

Overall, at first, I thought it would be a tedious and monotonous GED course. However, Tasmia ma’am proved me wrong totally by her unique teaching style and knowledge. I have learned a lot by taking POL101 under TmN ma’am, and it never felt like I had put effort. It was one of the most engaging and enjoyable course of my bachelor life and I will miss our beloved TmN ma’am always.

So make sure you pay attention to her lectures, go through the slides thoroughly. She is quite serious about the presentation as well. Try to interact with her and participate as much as possible

The slides must be very good to look at, the contents must be clear and well informed. Also communicate with her in the classroom. If you can do all this, then you’ll surely end up with a good grade.

aud.review:
POL101 - AUD (Dr. Anas Ansar)
Anas sir is probably the most easygoing faculty for this course. He tries to make his classes engaging and doesn’t burden students with unnecessary pressure. He takes three quizzes and counts the best two. The quizzes consist of MCQs and fill-in-the-blank questions. There’s only one mid, which consists of short questions. The final consists of both short and broad questions. He gives suggestions for these beforehand. There’s a fairly basic group assignment. This semester, he didn’t take any presentations; instead, he took a viva, which was very straightforward as well. Just a heads-up, he won’t be available in Fall 2026, and I’m not exactly sure when he’ll be back at NSU to teach again.
